newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Blade link seen in Malaysia helicopter crash-paper.
newsitem.headline: Blade link seen in Malaysia helicopter crash-paper.

text.p: The crash of the helicopter which killed the head of Malaysian car maker Proton Bhd may have been caused by two rotor blades coming off, a local newspaper reported on Thursday.

The New Straits Times newspaper quoted the head of the Department of Civil Aviation as saying he believed the Agusta 109 helicopter belonging to the DRB-Hicom group of companies, lost altitude when the blades came off.

"This is based on the recovery of two of the blades about 50 metres from the crash site. One was retrieved from a fish pond and another under a coconut tree," Yahaya Abdul Rahman was quoted as saying. He is heading a four-man investigation team into the accident which occurred on Monday.
The helicopter went down in eastern Pahang state in a fiery crash which scattered blackened debris in a rubber estate.
An official at the Department of Civil Aviation declined on Thursday to comment on the article.
Yahaya Ahmad, chairman of Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd (Proton), perished in the crash along with his wife and the pilot of the helicopter.
